summary: This is a justified, low-novelty port: it swaps the merge branch's c320 V1 (19.71 us at full decode_1) for combo-b1's gated V0..V4 chain, which routed V3 at 0.791 in 8713665f and scored 17.39 us. Every row is already measured, so no companion is needed. The predicted ~1.545 is only about +1.0% over the 1.5295 best, inside run noise, so read the result row by row and from the PATH CHOSEN lines, not from the headline.
justification: A. The mechanism is measured, not inferred. In 8713665f the chain gate printed 'V3 (A+C) 18.98 us vs V0 24.00 us head to head, ratio 0.791; pass 1: V0 24.00, V1 21.41, V2 21.18, V3 18.91, V4 18.91', and the judged full decode_1 row was 17.39 us (c320_attn_kernel<320,true> 11.4 + combine 4.2). The merge run a78f29ae carried only V1 (its gate printed c320 21.6 vs two-level 24.0, ratio 0.900) and scored 19.71 us. Expect full decode_1 near 17.4-17.6 us, about -2.3 us x weight 16. The kernel is still about 4x its 4.3 us SoL, so this is a launch-chain gain, not a floor claim. The other two rows are the merge's own measured wins and are kept unchanged: sliding decode_1 11.05 (best 12.1, master per-kvhead 10.87) and SV32 28.02 (best 29.01). Arithmetic: 1.5347 x (1 + about 0.75% from the decode_1 load) gives about 1.545, matching the hypothesis. The expected directions and baselines are consistent: full decode_1 is faster than the merge but about flat against the best, which already had V3. sliding decode_1 and verify_32 are faster than the best. Everything else is flat. The prior is accurate and not a duplicate: merge-perkvhead-c320-sv32-tiled ported only V1, this ports V3/V4, and combo-b1 is not on the do-not-try list (DIAGNOSIS action 3(i) names exactly this merge). Weakest link: the headline. The whole expected gain over the best (~+1.0-1.3%) sits at or below the ~1.24% one-run margin and the ±1.5% per-row noise, so a single check can confirm the stack only through the three rows (FD1 ~17.4, SD1 ~11.0, SV32 ~28.0) and the PATH CHOSEN lines. The second weak link is port fidelity. The two branches use different route mechanisms (merge: `_C320_ROUTE` bool + `_IMPORT_T0` + shared `_cx_*` helpers that GATE B also uses; combo-b1: `_C320_FN` + `IMPORT_T0` as the module's first statement + its own `_c320_*` phases). Deleting the merge's c320 code must not delete the `_cx_clock`/`_cx_may_start`/`_cx_interleaved`/`_cx_phase_b` helpers that SV32's GATE B needs.
confounders: sliding-decode1-cluster-per-kvhead (master 5d528bf3): disjoint row (SD1), but it is the reason the merge beats combo-b1 at SD1. Its `_slide_init` / `_sd_setup_body` route.pop(1) and the `_SD_ROUTE` freeze must stay byte-identical. If SD1 reads ~12 us or the '[slide] PATH CHOSEN: sliding B=1 PERHEAD ON' line is missing, that is a merge error, not a result.
full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (V0 comparator at FD1): unchanged on 5d528bf3 vs combo-b1's base 7e12891 (both gates printed V0 24.00 us), so the 0.791 ratio carries over unconfounded.

restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn (master skF FUSED_PRE at 1<B<=64): a different fused prologue, a different kernel and module, and no runtime interaction at B=1. The name collision is a risk: the slug's 'v3chain' (combo-b1 variant V3) is not master's 'v3 fused pre-attn'. The builder must port combo-b1's c320 FUSED code, not copy master's skF B>1 prologue layout.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup (master _pre_attention_kernel): V3 reproduces its unpaired B=1 full-layer semantics (RMSNorm, no RoPE, e4m3, k/v scale) inside kernel A and writes the cache row itself. Any mismatch shows up as a GATE A stored-row failure, which sends the class to V0/V1 rather than causing a timing confound. The SV32 tiled kernel replaces this kernel's launch only at SV32 and is self-attributed by GATE B.
interference: No companion is warranted. Every piece is shape-gated to a different row (FD1: combo-b1 chain; SD1: master per-kvhead; SV32: tiled pre-attention). Each piece prints its own in-run A/B (the chain prints V0..V4 numbers plus a head-to-head; GATE B prints pre and step times), and there are judged references for every row: master 4b608df5 (FD1 22.70, SD1 10.87, SV32 28.83), merge a78f29ae (19.71 / 11.05 / 28.02) and combo-b1 8713665f (17.39 / 12.1 / 29.01). A gain or a loss is therefore attributable row by row in one run. An ab-revert of per-kvhead would reproduce 8713665f. A control with V1 only would reproduce a78f29ae. Neither tells us anything new, and both spend a check that DIAGNOSIS wants moved to the verify wgmma line.
rules_flags: None blocking. kernel_fn paths are unchanged from two judged runs: config-only FD1/SV32 predicates on route state frozen at import; c320 workspaces torch.empty sized from page_table.shape[1] and batch; no per-state device pointers (c320 holds only host bools; PDL decided once at import, no per-call fallback flag); FP8 KV, e4m3 q, fp32 merges, bf16 out; every key attended (the fused path overwrites only the new key's smem slot with the same e4m3 bytes it stores to the cache).

The FUSED kernel A writes k/v cache at cache_loc inside the timed call. That is required and allowed (it replaces the pre-attention store). GATE A's stored-row check (<= 3/128 bytes differ vs _pre_attention_kernel, other rows unchanged) must be ported with it, not dropped.

BUILD hygiene: the brief adds 'TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a'. If it is set via os.environ at import, set it only around the c320 load_inline and restore it afterwards, so a later phase cannot silently rebuild a master module.
open_questions: New refusal rule vs verbatim port: the brief adds 'refuse a variant with local bytes > 0', which combo-b1 never applied. The 8713665f log prints no regs/local-bytes line for the c320 instantiations, so it is unknown whether A<320,FUSED=true> (it builds q MMA fragments in registers) spills. If it does, this rule silently drops V3/V4 and the run degrades to the merge's V1 (~19.7 us), which wastes the check. Either print local bytes but do not refuse V3/V4 on it (they already passed on the judge), or have the builder check ptxas -v output if any nvcc is reachable.

V3 and V4 tied in pass 1 (18.91 vs 18.91 us), so the routed variant can be either. Readout: name the routed variant from the PATH CHOSEN chain line. Either is a success at FD1 ~17.4-17.6 us. A FD1 row near 19.5-19.7 with V3/V4 routed would mean the merged base breaks the chain gain. A row near 22.7 means GATE A fell back.

Gate standard vs today's LESSON (two interleaved rounds >= 1.03 with IQR): the chain gate (0.791) clears any standard. The SV32 GATE B routed at step ratio 0.975 (1.026x single round) in a78f29ae, which is below the new 1.03 bar. It has gone live and gained on the judge in three runs (b9d062aa 27.92, 52cbfaeb 27.42, a78f29ae 28.02 vs ~28.8-29.0). Keep it exactly as on the merge branch, as the brief says. Do not retrofit the 1.03 rule here, or SV32 will likely fall back and the run loses its verify_32 row.

Import clock: merge ended its phases at 222.8 s and combo-b1's chain finished at 179 s on a base without the PERHEAD build. combo-b1's module (FUSED + PDL variants, with a FUSED-fail rebuild path) is larger than the V1-only module. Expect the chain phase to end around 250-280 s, well within the 480 s start rule. Confirm only one muse_full_decode_c320 load_inline appears in the log; two modules with the same name and different sources would be a build-cache hazard.

Submit gating: at ~1.545 predicted vs 1.5295 best, a single check will not prove a new best. Treat it as the stacking base for sliding-verify1-pseudo-fused-preattn-rope (DIAGNOSIS action 3(ii)), and promote it to a scored submit only together with that stacked change, or if the check rows all land as predicted.
